A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Eso-LMs research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and pagination.

before.justification: V3 reports original Eso-LMs experiments on LM1B and OWT, including perplexity, generation quality, latency, and ablation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains those experiments and adds estimator-variance measurements, MDLM importance-weighted likelihood evaluation, a synthetic Markov experiment, and XSum conditional-generation results.

M1.justification: The hybrid objective, attention mechanisms, KV caching, training and sampling algorithms, and improved block sampler are retained. Applying existing checkpoints and likelihood estimators in additional evaluations does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V4 substantially broadens task coverage beyond likelihood evaluation and unconditional generation by adding XSum conditional generation in Appendix E.14. Appendix E.1 also introduces synthetic first-order Markov data with vocabulary size 254 and sequence length 30. Existing language-modeling and zero-shot datasets remain.

E2.justification: MDLM now participates in the importance-weighted likelihood comparison, previously reported only for Eso-LMs. Appendix E.14 also adds FLAN-T5-Small as a scored XSum reference, reporting 0.42 rescaled BertScore without a corresponding latency. Existing benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include 10K-step XSum fine-tuning, diffusion steps T={1,4,8,16,32}, and rescaled BertScore comparisons under latency budgets. V4 also evaluates MDLM with K={1,10,20,50,100,1000} sampled orderings and compares NELBO estimators on one OWT sequence. Previously stated protocols for retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds focused checks of NELBO-estimator variance, MDLM likelihood estimates versus sampled-ordering count, and likelihood-bound tightness on synthetic Markov data. Existing attention, batch-split, sampling-schedule, and long-context analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Table 2 reports estimator means and standard deviations over 100 trials on one OWT sequence, using ten Monte Carlo samples per trial for L_MDM and one for L_AO. Existing latency uncertainty reporting remains unchanged; no increase in training-seed replication is documented.

E6.justification: V4 adds MDLM IW perplexities from 31.19 at K=1 to 26.82 at K=1000, estimator means/SDs of 3.25/0.56 and 3.28/0.03, and Markov results near NLL 1.73. Table 16 adds XSum results: under 0.1 seconds, Eso-LM scores 0.19 at T=8 versus MDLM's -0.06 at T=1. Previously reported numerical results are retained; these are additional evaluations rather than same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, the NELBO and importance-weighted derivations in Appendix B, and the formal attention definitions are unchanged. New Appendix E.1 discusses the existing distinction between a likelihood bound and equality, without adding a formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about AR–MDM interpolation, exact KV caching with parallel generation, likelihood estimation, and unconditional speed–quality performance remain. The abstract omits the numerical long-context speedups, but the introduction retains them. The title change does not redefine the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: V4 qualifies the previous assertion that baseline IW evaluation is intractable by identifying short LM1B sequences as feasible. It adds interpretation of the retained zero-shot results, explicitly noting the AR–Eso-LM–MDLM ordering on four of seven datasets, and argues that near-tight likelihood bounds on simple synthetic data need not remain tight at scale.

D1.justification: V4 supplies fine-tuning steps, hardware, a preprocessing reference, and sampling information for XSum, plus ordering counts and batch size for the new MDLM IW evaluation. Existing implementation and resource-access information remains. Table 6 introduces an unresolved documentation inconsistency: it labels the experiment LM1B but mentions the OWT test set.

R1.justification: V4 adds a critical discussion of Kong et al. (2023), reports adoption of its estimator in Wang et al. (2025b), and cites subsequent scaling work by Sahoo et al. (2026). It also expands distinctions from approximate KV-caching approaches and adds references supporting the XSum experiment. The established research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V4 retitles the paper 'A Family of Any-Order Diffusion LLMs', updates authorship and publication text, shortens the abstract, and makes targeted paragraph revisions. The generative-perplexity subsection moves from E.3 to E.8; the main narrative and most appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 redraws and transposes Figure 1, enlarges Figure 3 into a two-column display, and adds Tables 2, 6, and 16. Figure 17 and several appendix displays move or resize with revised page breaks. Existing plots and generated examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens the empirical support for likelihood estimation through the variance check and direct MDLM IW evaluation, while adding conditional-generation evidence on XSum. These gains are limited by the single-sequence variance study, sparse details for the new experiments, and the LM1B/OWT inconsistency in Table 6. Overall, the added validation provides a modest net improvement while preserving the established results.
